full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the petitioner herein as the pre-emptor filed an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Companygonj, Noakhali stating, inter alia, that he is a co-sharer tenant to the case holding by way of inheritance and purchase. Because of misunderstanding the seller respondent No. 2 Rai Mohan Das (full brother of the pre-emptor) without serving any notice upon the pre-emptor transferred the case land to pre-emptees by a registered deed of sale dated 05.06.2002. The pre-emptees are strangers to the case holding. After obtaining the certified copy of the deed of sale, the pre-emptor definitely came to know about the Sale of the case land on 05.01.2003 and hence the case for pre-emption. 

 3. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as the pre-emptees contested the pre-emption case by filing a written objection denying all the material statements of the application for pre-emption contending, inter alia, that the pre-emption application was not maintainable in its form. It was bad for defect of parties. The pre-emptees specific case is that before transferring the case land, seller respondent No.3 offered the case land to the pre-emptor on whose refusal, the pre-emptees agreed to purchase the case land and accordingly a bainapatra was executed and thereafter, pre-emptee No. 1 published a legal notice through his learned lawyer in the local newspaper. As per said legal notice neither the pre-emptor nor any other co-sharer came forward to purchase the case land and in such background the seller transferred the case land to the pre-emptees by a registered deed of sale dated 05.06.2002 and as such the pre-emptor waived his right of pre-emption by refusing to purchase the case land.
